stories.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN
stories.summary: CVE-2026-104935 affects Ivanti Connect Secure and it can be exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution with elevated privileges.
stories.explanation: An attacker found a flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure (a VPN appliance that controls access to company networks) that lets them run commands with root privileges (maximum access) without even logging in, and this works even on systems with the latest security patches applied. This matters because VPN appliances are often a first entry point into corporate networks, so complete bypass means attackers can gain deep access. Defenders respond by applying emergency patches immediately, blocking suspicious traffic patterns, and checking logs to see if the flaw was exploited.

stories.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway.
stories.explanation: Ivanti discovered that someone was actively using a previously unknown security flaw in their Connect Secure VPN product to break in, and they told all customers to patch right away. This matters because active exploitation means real attacks are happening now, not just theoretical scenarios. Defenders prioritize this above other work, apply patches as fast as possible, and watch for signs of compromise on their systems.

stories.title: Citrix, Fortinet, Ivanti Patch 29 Vulnerabilities Across Their Products
stories.summary: Critical-severity flaws could lead to authentication bypass, code execution, and sensitive authentication information leaks.
stories.explanation: Citrix, Fortinet, and Ivanti all released patches for 29 security flaws, some of which are critical—meaning attackers could skip login checks, run their own code, or steal authentication details used to verify user identity. This matters because defenders need to patch multiple vendor products and a delay in any one of them leaves that system exposed. Defenders create a patch schedule across all three vendors, test patches in a safe environment first, then roll them out in order of severity.

stories.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
stories.summary: An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity. Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti,
stories.explanation: A security researcher found that attackers were chaining three separate zero-day flaws (previously unknown vulnerabilities) in Ivanti Connect Secure together to gain root access without authentication, but Ivanti has only released fixes for two of them so far. This matters because until all three are patched, attackers can still exploit the unfixed one to regain access. Defenders apply the two available patches immediately, isolate affected systems or disable the VPN if possible, and wait urgently for the third patch.

stories.title: Microsoft October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,411 flaws, 3 zero-days
stories.summary: Today is Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,411 flaws, including one actively exploited and two publicly disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities.
stories.explanation: Microsoft released security updates on their monthly Patch Tuesday that fix 1,411 separate vulnerabilities, which is unusually high, and three of these are zero-days (one is already being exploited in real attacks, two are public knowledge but not yet widely exploited). This matters because the huge number means organizations have a lot of testing and deployment work, and the exploited zero-day requires fastest attention. Defenders prioritize the exploited zero-day, test patches for critical systems first, and deploy in waves to minimize disruption.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Vulnerabilities, Including Exploited Windows Zero-Day
stories.summary: The most important is CVE-2026-96951, a security feature bypass flaw in Windows that has been exploited in the wild.
stories.explanation: Microsoft released patches for 1,413 security flaws, with CVE-2026-96951 being a Windows security feature bypass that attackers are already using in real attacks. This matters because Windows runs on most corporate machines, so this flaw is high-value for attackers. Defenders deploy this patch to all Windows systems as their top priority, often within hours, and monitor for signs of exploitation.

stories.title: Ghostscript flaw lets hackers hijack servers via PDF uploads
stories.summary: A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-39919) in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine could allow remote code execution through specially crafted PDF files.
stories.explanation: A critical flaw in Ghostscript (a PDF processing tool used by many servers) allows an attacker to craft a malicious PDF file that, when the server processes it, can run arbitrary commands and take over the server. This matters because many organizations automatically process PDFs from users (converting formats, extracting text, etc.), creating an easy attack vector. Defenders apply the patch immediately, restrict PDF uploads if possible, and scan for suspicious PDF files that may have been uploaded.

stories.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested for Allegedly Planting Hidden Recorder in Executive Conference Room
stories.summary: A Saudi National and employee of OpenAI has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to covertly record sensitive conversations. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. He was arrested by
stories.explanation: An OpenAI employee was arrested for secretly planting a hidden recording device in a conference room to capture sensitive conversations, which is a physical security and insider threat incident rather than a cyber attack. This matters because it shows that security risks come from people, not just software, and that executives and sensitive projects can be targeted by insiders. Defenders respond by reviewing physical security controls, conducting insider threat training, and investigating whether any confidential information was compromised.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-5477 is a data processing error in ISC BIND (DNS software that translates domain names to IP addresses), which is old and likely already patched in modern systems. This matters mainly as a historical reference or if legacy systems are still running unpatched versions. Defenders check if any systems still run vulnerable BIND versions and update them, as DNS compromise can redirect users to malicious sites.

cves.explanation: CVE-2015-3306 is an improper access control flaw in ProFTPD (file transfer software), meaning someone could access files they shouldn't be allowed to, and this is an older vulnerability likely already addressed. This matters if legacy file servers still run old ProFTPD versions without patches. Defenders inventory all FTP systems, patch or replace vulnerable versions, and restrict FTP usage in favor of more secure alternatives.

cves.explanation: CVE-2016-3081 is a command injection flaw in Apache Struts (a Java web framework), allowing attackers to run their own commands through specially crafted web requests, and this is from 2016 so most systems have moved past it. This matters if any web applications built with old Struts versions are still in production. Defenders check if their Java applications use vulnerable Struts versions, apply patches or updates, and run web application firewalls to block injection attempts.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. cves.explanation: CVE-2026-104935 is an authentication bypass flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure versions newer than 22.7R2.14 but before 25.1.3.0, allowing remote attackers to run arbitrary commands without logging in. This matters because it affects the range of Ivanti versions most organizations are likely running, creating widespread exposure. Defenders apply the patch to version 25.1.3.0 or later immediately, or implement network-level restrictions if patching is delayed.

cves.explanation: CVE-2026-104286 is a path traversal flaw in Fortinet FortiMail (email security appliance), which means an attacker can read or modify files outside the intended directory, potentially accessing sensitive data or configuration files. This matters because email gateways see all incoming and outgoing messages, so compromise could expose confidential communications. Defenders apply Fortinet's patch immediately and review email gateway logs for suspicious file access patterns.
